inputs.original_text: Her 2026 State of the State agenda would make gunmakers share responsibility for preventing weapons sold in New York from being easily converted into illegal machine guns. That matters: communities should not be left to absorb the harm when an industry could take foreseeable risks seriously. The proposal also includes criminal penalties, but the account doesn’t say who would face them—a detail that will matter for whether accountability reaches the industry or falls elsewhere.
inputs.modified_text: Her 2026 State of the State agenda would make gunmakers share responsibility for weapons sold in New York being converted into illegal machine guns—and adds criminal penalties without saying who would face them. Preventing violence is a serious concern, but vague penalties and shifting responsibility onto an entire industry are no substitute for holding those who break the law accountable. The public deserves to know whether this is really aimed at manufacturers or whether the burden could spread to people who obey the law.

rationales.entity_drift: The central actors and setting remain the same; people who obey the law are newly introduced as a possible affected group.
rationales.relation_drift: The original specifies shared responsibility for preventing easy conversion; the modified wording instead assigns responsibility for weapons being converted and raises the possibility of burdening lawful people.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text contains no clear internal contradiction.
